Perusal of the chargesheet reveals that after registration of FIR, the IO has recorded statement of Dharmender, as an eye witness of the incident.

As per tehrir, as recorded by the IO, the said witness has seen the accident in question and he stated in his statement dated 14.04.2015, that the accident has taken place, as the victim was hit by the offending vehicle, which was negligently driven by R1.
He further stated in his statement that initially R1 was apprehended by him and he disclosed his name as Lakhan Singh but, he started the offending vehicle and fled away.

Though, the petitioners failed to examine the said eye witness in support of their case, however, it is trite law that in Motor Accident Claims Cases, the standard of proof is not as strict as the standard of proof to be adopted in criminal matters, and non-examination of eye witness or even if the eye witness turned hostile before the Tribunal, the same cannot be treated as fatal, in a claim for compensation, in respect of road traffic accident, if the factum of rashness and negligent stands proved on the basis of other reliable evidence produced by the petitioners.

, it can be safely concluded that the proceedings before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) cannot be rejected, merely on account of non-examination of eye witness,

However, as per their record, no renewal fee was found to be deposited by R1, after the date of initial issuance of driving license in favour of R1, for the period 21.11.2002 till 20.11.2005.
Thus, the driving license in favour of R1 was invalid, as on the date of accident LRs of Vishnu Vs Lakhan Singh and Ors.
Thus, the insurance company/R4 has discharged the initial onus of proving that the license of R1 was not valid on the date of accident.
The onus has now shifted upon R1 to prove that the report Ex.R3W1/1 was a fake report but, no endeavour was made by R1, to summon any witness from the concerned department i.e. ARTO Farrukhabad UP, to prove the said report as fake.
Thus, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the DL of R1, as on the date of accident was not valid and consequently, there is breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy by the insured.
Thus, the insurance Company/R4 is entitled to seek recovery rights but, after paying the compensation amount to the claimants.
However, as per decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in case titled as Naveen Kumar vs Vijay Kumar and others in Civil Appeal No. 1427 of 2018 (arising out of SLP(C) No. 18943 of 2016), decided on 06.02.2018, the person whose name is reflected in the records of the registering authority is the owner within the meaning of Section 2(30) of M.V. Act and thus liable to compensate.
In facts and as per settled law as discussed above, since the offending vehicle was duly insured with the insurance company/R4, hence R4 is liable to pay the entire compensation amount to the petitioners as per law and thereafter, insurance company/R4 is entitled to seek recovery of the said amount from R1 and R3, who are jointly and severally liable to indemnify the insurance company/R4.
49.
R4 is directed to deposit the awarded amount of Rs. 17,83,898/- within 30 days from today within the jurisdiction of this Tribunal, that is, State Bank of India, Rohini Courts Branch, Delhi along with interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till notice of deposition of the awarded amount to be given by R4 to the petitioners and his advocates and to show or deposit the receipt of the acknowledgement with the Nazir as per rules.
